title: Geometric base change of the inverse orientation factor
statement: Fix P, separated finite-type k0-models X0,Y0 and a separated finite-type f0 whose geometric base change f is smooth of pure relative dimension d. Let Q=gX* and R=gY*, b the specified gamma(zeta)-normalized source comparison [def-pur-finite-geometric-purity-coordinates]. For every fixed-scalar pro-etale complex M on Y, use the factors a_M, comparison S_M and canonical unit exceptional exchange e_omega of [lem-pur-finite-geometric-purity-factorization]. Then Q(a_M);S_M;(1 tensor e_omega)=b_M;a_(RM). This concerns the normalized inverse diagonal orientation, the tensor/shift comparisons and the root line, with no tensor counit transpose theta or exceptional exchange at M.

source.place: Geometric base change of the inverse orientation factor

proof.text: Retag by Spec gamma. The underlying sites and compactification are unchanged, as is the normalized diagonal orientation under the counit-preserving exceptional comparison. Apply the finite orientation clause of finite_factors to this k-linear square, transport from its canonical pullback to the actual Cartesian Frobenius square, and undo comparison. The resulting unit exceptional exchange is e_omega by its explicit ordinary-unit formula.

Identify the finite-general-ring orientation with the direct-A diagonal orientation. The level projection from the integral root line gives the same finite twist; roots-of-unity inverse image is transition compatible and sends zeta to gamma(zeta). Thus the tensor/shift source comparison is the existing b in every primitive-root chart, including degree zero.

Tensor the inverse-orientation equation by the pulled-back f* input. Tensor naturality and the inverse-image square yield S; conjugate by u_M and u_RM and reassociate the shift. This is exactly Q(a_M);S_M;(1 tensor e_omega)=b_M;a_RM.

theorem geometricPurityOrientation_exchange
    (M : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))) :
    (P.smoothPurityPullback (P.frobeniusGaloisMap X₀)).map
        (P.geometricPurityOrientationFactor (P.frobeniusMap f₀)
          (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).hom d M) ≫
      (P.geometricPurityTensorSquare (P.frobeniusMap f₀) (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).hom
        (P.frobeniusGaloisMap X₀) (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀)
        (P.field.frobenius_square_cartesian X₀ Y₀ f₀).2.2.2.2.1 M).hom ≫
      ((smoothPurityTensor P.Coefficient (P.frobeniusFiber X₀).left).obj
        ((P.smoothPurityPullback (P.frobeniusMap f₀)).obj
          (P.geometricPurityRealized (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left
            ((P.smoothPurityPullback (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀)).obj M)))).map
        (P.geometricPurityDualizingExchange (P.frobeniusMap f₀)
          (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).hom (P.frobeniusGaloisMap X₀)
          (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀)
          (P.field.frobenius_square_cartesian X₀ Y₀ f₀).2.2.2.2.2.1) =
    (P.geometricPuritySource X₀ Y₀ f₀ d M).hom ≫
      P.geometricPurityOrientationFactor (P.frobeniusMap f₀) (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).hom d
        ((P.smoothPurityPullback (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀)).obj M)
